questions.question: You have modules that depend on each other, so changing one forces changes in the others. What is this problem called, and what is a potential solution?
options: Cohesion – use an anticohesive design pattern
Encapsulation – use a SOLID principle so modules do not encapsulate each other
Coupling – refactor to loose coupling using inversion of control and dependency injection
Dependency – use polymorphism and abstraction so the module functions on its own
questions.answer: Coupling – refactor to loose coupling using inversion of control and dependency injection

questions.question: Which statement best describes the Liskov substitution principle?
options: A class should have only a single responsibility
Software entities should be open for extension, but closed for modification
Many client-specific interfaces are better than one general-purpose interface
Objects in a program should be replaceable with instances of their subtypes without altering the correctness of the program
questions.answer: Objects in a program should be replaceable with instances of their subtypes without altering the correctness of the program

questions.question: What is the difference between an interface and an abstract class?
options: Interfaces can contain code or data; abstract classes cannot. A class can inherit from many abstract classes but implement only one interface
Interfaces can contain code or data; abstract classes cannot. A class can inherit from one abstract class but implement unlimited interfaces
Abstract classes can contain code or data; interfaces cannot. A class can inherit from one abstract class but implement unlimited interfaces
Abstract classes can contain code or data; interfaces cannot. A class can inherit from many abstract classes but implement only one interface
questions.answer: Abstract classes can contain code or data; interfaces cannot. A class can inherit from one abstract class but implement unlimited interfaces

questions.question: The open/closed principle states that classes should be open for extension but closed for ______.
Which choice is a disadvantage of inheritance?
options: Overridden methods of the parent class cannot be reused
Responsibilities are not evenly distributed between parent and child classes
Classes related by inheritance are tightly coupled to each other
The internal state of the parent class is accessible to its children
questions.answer: Classes related by inheritance are tightly coupled to each other

questions.question: In C++, which statement is TRUE about the virtual keyword used with destructors?
options: A virtual destructor prevents object slicing automatically
A virtual destructor ensures dynamic binding for all member functions of the class
A virtual destructor allows correct destruction of derived objects through a base class pointer
A virtual destructor makes the class abstract automatically
questions.answer: A virtual destructor allows correct destruction of derived objects through a base class pointer

questions.question: If a language implements only pass-by-value for function parameters, can an object parameter be set to a new instance inside the function so that the new value is seen by the caller?
options: Yes, but only if it is a reference and not a primitive class
Yes, since the value is a reference even though it is passed by value
No, you will get a compilation error
No, a local copy is initialized and is lost as soon as it goes out of scope
questions.answer: No, a local copy is initialized and is lost as soon as it goes out of scope

questions.question: In C++, RAII stands for Resource Acquisition Is ______.
A superheroes table has columns name, alias, power1, power2, power3. What is the right step to normalize it?
options: Create a lookup table for powers (code, description) and a junction table of superhero names and power codes
Add a record identifier column and make it the primary key
Add more columns power4, power5 and so on
Replace the power columns with one column and add one record per hero-power combination
questions.answer: Create a lookup table for powers (code, description) and a junction table of superhero names and power codes

questions.question: Which MySQL feature runs multiple SQL statements as a single unit that can be rolled back entirely if there is an error?
options: Temporary table
Transaction
Event scheduler
Trigger

questions.question: What is the primary use of EXPLAIN ANALYZE in MySQL 8.0.18 and later?
options: To display user privileges on the database
To validate SQL syntax before execution
To execute the query and display real execution time with the query plan
To show estimated cost without executing the query
questions.answer: To execute the query and display real execution time with the query plan

questions.question: In a SELECT query, WHERE filters rows, while the ______ clause filters groups based on aggregate function results.
In MySQL, a ______ JOIN returns all rows from the left table and the matching rows from the right table, filling NULL where there is no match.
What is true about indexes?
options: They speed up read access while slowing down writes
They secure the database from intruders
They speed up reads and writes
They speed up write access while slowing down reads
questions.answer: They speed up read access while slowing down writes

questions.question: What is the purpose of an arbiter in a MongoDB replica set?
options: It monitors the replica set and sends email on failure
It casts the tie-breaking vote in an election
It holds a backup copy of the database
It reboots the failed server
questions.answer: It casts the tie-breaking vote in an election

questions.question: Inside an UPDATE trigger in MySQL, the new value of the address column is accessed with ______.address
After an insertion into an AVL tree, a node has balance factor +2 (left-heavy) and its left child has balance factor -1 (right-heavy). Which rebalancing is needed?
options: Single right rotation
Single left rotation
Left-Right double rotation
Right-Left double rotation

questions.question: To find the k largest elements from a stream of n numbers using a priority queue, what is the best approach and time complexity?
options: Max-heap of all n elements – O(n log n)
Min-heap of size k – O(n log k)
Sorted array with insertion – O(n k)
Min-heap of size n – O(n)
questions.answer: Min-heap of size k – O(n log k)

questions.question: What is the optimal time complexity to count subarrays whose sum equals k in an integer array (negatives allowed)?
options: O(n) using prefix sums and a hash map
O(n) using a sliding window
O(n log n) using sorting
O(n²) is the best possible
questions.answer: O(n) using prefix sums and a hash map

questions.question: The sliding window maximum problem can be solved in O(n) using a monotonic ______ (double-ended queue).
Dynamic programming applies when a problem has optimal substructure and ______ subproblems.
Dijkstra’s algorithm can give wrong results when a graph has negative edge weights. Which algorithm handles them (and detects negative cycles)?
options: Prim’s algorithm
Kruskal’s algorithm
Bellman-Ford algorithm
Breadth-first search

questions.question: A topological ordering of vertices exists only if the graph is a directed ______ graph (give the full name or the abbreviation).
Which combination gives O(1) get and put for an LRU cache?
options: Array and binary search
Hash map and doubly linked list
Min-heap and hash set
Balanced BST and queue
questions.answer: Hash map and doubly linked list

questions.question: What is the time complexity of merging n overlapping intervals (unsorted input)?
options: O(n)
O(n log n)
O(n²)
O(log n)
